tutorial.intro.title: What FocusMic does
tutorial.intro.subtitle: The camera locks onto your mouth; the microphone captures the sound.
tutorial.intro.body: It processes the microphone signal: your voice stays, nearby voices are suppressed as much as possible. Everything runs on this PC; camera and microphone content is never uploaded.
tutorial.prep.title: Before you start
tutorial.prep.subtitle: A little preparation makes separation much steadier.
tutorial.prep.b1: Keep your whole face in frame with even lighting. Do not cover your mouth with your hand, hair or a mask.
tutorial.prep.b2: Place the microphone close to your mouth; a headset microphone is usually steadier than a desktop one.
tutorial.prep.b3: Headphones are recommended. Speakers will be picked up by the microphone again.
tutorial.prep.b4: Close other apps that use the camera or GPU so they do not compete for resources.
tutorial.first.title: First time
tutorial.first.subtitle: Follow these steps in order and you should be ready.
tutorial.first.s1: Open FocusMic and choose your microphone and camera on Home.
tutorial.first.s2: Click Start separation and wait for the status chip to say Running.
tutorial.first.s2d: A mouth box appearing in the preview means your face is locked.
tutorial.first.s3: If no mouth box appears, adjust your position and lighting, then click Re-lock target.
tutorial.first.s4: Open your voice or meeting app and set its microphone to CABLE Output.
tutorial.first.s4d: That is the virtual audio device output used by FocusMic.
tutorial.first.s5: Disable that app's noise suppression, automatic gain and echo cancellation.
tutorial.first.s5d: Otherwise it will process the separated audio a second time.
tutorial.first.s6: Turn on Live headphone monitoring if you want to listen to yourself.
tutorial.states.title: Status and bypass
tutorial.states.subtitle: Read the status chip before deciding whether to intervene.
tutorial.states.b3: Bypass: when your mouth is covered, the target is lost or you switch manually, the raw microphone is used; separation resumes automatically when the target returns.
tutorial.states.b4: Press Ctrl+Alt+M or click Bypass on Home to toggle manually; you can change the shortcut in Settings.
tutorial.states.b5: If the microphone, camera or virtual audio device disconnects, FocusMic stops automatically. Reconnect it, select the device again and start.
tutorial.states.b6: Adjust output gain before starting; it takes effect on the next start.
tutorial.tips.title: Make it more accurate
tutorial.tips.subtitle: Most problems are pose, distance or lighting.
tutorial.tips.b1: A visible mouth matters most. After turning your head, wait 1–2 seconds for the picture to catch up.
tutorial.tips.b2: If other people are in frame, click Select target while running and box your own face in the preview.
tutorial.tips.b3: The noisier the room, the closer your mouth should be to the microphone; this helps more than post-processing.
tutorial.tips.b4: Falcon Small has lower latency and suits daily use; Falcon Big is cleaner but uses more GPU and adds latency.
tutorial.tips.b5: If your voice is suppressed too much or audio and video drift, adjust A/V sync, starting around 20–40 ms.
tutorial.faq.title: Common questions
tutorial.faq.subtitle: Try these first; they usually solve the problem.
tutorial.faq.q1: There is no mouth box and tracking stays at 0%?
tutorial.faq.a1: Check whether another app is using the camera, whether the light is too dim, and whether your face or mouth is covered. Then click Re-lock target.
tutorial.faq.q2: My voice app receives no sound?
tutorial.faq.a2: Make sure its microphone is CABLE Output, then check that CABLE Input on Home says connected.
tutorial.faq.q3: Other people hear my voice very quietly?
tutorial.faq.a3: Keep your mouth visible during separation and do not cover it. Move the microphone closer and check the tracking rate on the Performance page.
tutorial.faq.a4: Use Falcon Small first and close other GPU-heavy apps. The full-chain latency on the Performance page shows the live value.
tutorial.faq.q5: The Start button is grey after stopping?
tutorial.faq.a5: Wait for Stopping to finish; it usually returns to Idle within a second or two and the button recovers automatically.
tutorial.privacy.title: Privacy
tutorial.privacy.subtitle: No internet needed; nothing is uploaded.
tutorial.privacy.b1: Camera frames and microphone audio are processed only on this PC and are never uploaded.
tutorial.privacy.b2: There is no telemetry; settings and logs stay in your local user profile.
tutorial.privacy.b3: The separated audio goes through the local virtual audio device (CABLE); only the voice app you choose can receive it.

about.tagline: Keep the person on camera, not the whole room.
about.what.title: What it is
about.what.body: FocusMic is a local Windows audio-visual target speaker extraction tool: the camera reads lip motion and the microphone hears the sound, isolating your voice from other people speaking in the same room in real time.
about.effect.title: What it does
about.effect.body: It keeps your voice and suppresses nearby speakers. If your mouth is covered, you leave the frame or the target is lost, it automatically passes the raw microphone through so you are never muted. Falcon Small inference takes about 65–85 ms per 2 s window. In an internal same-voice test, the audio-only baseline measured 0.6 dB SIR; the lip-based route measured 15.1 dB. Real results depend on lighting, face angle, microphone distance and room acoustics.
about.noise.title: vs. noise suppression
about.noise.body: Traditional noise suppression (RNNoise, Krisp, NVIDIA Broadcast and similar) removes fans, keyboards and stationary noise, but cannot tell two people talking at once apart; many implementations keep or suppress both voices together. FocusMic does not rely on whether a voice sounds like noise. It uses lip motion in the picture to identify the target speaker, so it can favor you even when a roommate talks at the same time. It solves concurrent-speech separation, not just noise.
about.req.title: Requirements
about.req.body: Windows 10/11 x64; an NVIDIA GPU and a driver that supports CUDA 12.8; a camera; a microphone; VB-CABLE. Disk: about 590 MB for the app and 4.3 GB for the AI runtime. VRAM: about 384 MB (Small) or 567 MB (Big). 8 GB+ RAM recommended.
about.perf.title: Performance
about.perf.body: Tested on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB + Ryzen 9 7945HX. Falcon Small: about 67.6 ms per window and about 31% GPU at a 0.2 s hop; Falcon Big: about 74.8 ms. MediaPipe mouth tracking: about 10.8 ms per frame, about 27% of one CPU core at 25 fps. End-to-end latency is roughly 0.3–0.5 s, excluding the receiving app's buffer; the in-app full-chain estimate is shown live.
about.quick.title: Quick start
about.quick.body:
1. Install VB-CABLE.
2. Install FocusMic-Runtime, then FocusMic.
3. In the first-run wizard choose your microphone and camera; face the camera with your mouth visible.
4. In your voice or meeting app, set the microphone to CABLE Output and disable its noise suppression, AGC and echo cancellation.
5. Click Start separation in FocusMic. Cover your mouth or press Ctrl+Alt+M to bypass to the raw microphone.
about.privacy.title: Privacy
about.privacy.body: All inference runs locally. Camera frames are not saved or uploaded. There is no telemetry. Logs are written only to %LOCALAPPDATA%\FocusMic\logs on this PC.

onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to FocusMic
onboarding.welcome.body: FocusMic watches the camera and listens to the microphone at the same time: it recognizes you by lip motion, keeps your voice and suppresses the people next to you as much as possible.
onboarding.welcome.b1: The camera is used only to recognize your mouth; frames are not saved.
onboarding.welcome.b2: Audio and video are processed only on this PC and are never uploaded.
onboarding.welcome.b3: The separated result reaches your voice or meeting app through a local virtual audio device.
onboarding.devices.title: Choose your devices
onboarding.devices.body: Pick the microphone and camera you normally use. You can change them later on Home without running this wizard again.
onboarding.output.title: Connect to your voice app
onboarding.output.body: FocusMic sends the separated audio to the local virtual audio device. In your voice or meeting app, select CABLE Output as the microphone.
onboarding.output.missing: ● Virtual audio device not found. Install it, then click Recheck.
onboarding.output.hint: If the virtual audio device is not installed yet, install it and click Recheck. You can also finish now and configure it later on Home.
onboarding.ready.title: You're all set
onboarding.ready.body:
Settings are saved locally. Click Finish to return to Home, then click Start separation.
You can change devices on Home or read the Guide at any time.
